name: Hanglok-Tech VIR
full_name: Hanglok-Tech vascular interventional robot (distributed architecture with DSA vision-servoing co-pilot)
group: Hanglok-Tech Co. Ltd., with Southeast University, South China University of Technology, Macau University of Science and Technology, Guangzhou First People's Hospital
versions: wang2024_vision (CBS 2024, phantom in an interventional suite) -> zhu2026_bending (T-RO 2026, adds phantom paths and in vivo trials)
devices_driven: 0.014 in microwire, guide catheter (8 F sheath in phantom), microcatheter; contrast injection module
translation_detail: other: microwire by an electric-gripper clamp on a lead-screw carriage with reverse drive (alternate clamp/release); microcatheter by dual friction wheels with multitooth Shore A70 silicone sleeve; guide catheter by advance-rotation module with Y-valve
rotation_detail: Microwire twisted by the clamp ('guidewire twister', not friction wheels); guide catheter rotated through bevel gears and clutch
device_range: 0.014 in microwire (nominal 0.36 mm); catheter sizes N.R.
force_sensing: Pressure and torque sensors on USART ports of the embedded boards (zhu2026 Fig. 5); no force numbers reported in the sections read
haptics_leader: Hand-held controller with joystick and touch screen (no haptics described)
imaging_compat: Runs in a clinical angiography suite with DSA frames fed to the controller (X-ray)
sterility: Disinfected end effector; disposable contrast injector; further sterile-barrier detail N.R.
validation_detail: Phantom: six vascular paths. Animal: nine in vivo vessel-navigation trials in pigs under IACUC approval of 20 Feb 2024 (zhu2026).
key_numbers: Vision co-pilot lowered the mean maximum bending-risk value 113.0 -> 49.0 in phantom (-56.6 %) and 239.8 -> 80.5 in animals (-66.4 %) (zhu2026 abstract)
